Hi Ellen —

Thanks for the clear list. I want to be explicit on our guarantees and the practical retention mechanics so your SOC can assess the risk model. Below are the key commitments and caveats (we can put any of these into binding contract language):

1) No-training commitment
- Redwood does not use customer content (requests, responses, attachments) to train models for any public or internal model updates. This is captured in our standard DPA and a separate signed attestation (attached).
- We may use heavily aggregated, de-identified telemetry (token counts, latency histograms) for platform performance research; these do NOT contain customer content and cannot be used to improve model outputs.

2) Operational data categories & default windows
- Ephemeral inference state (KV cache/prefix caches): default TTL = 24 hours, purged automatically. Can be configured shorter.
- Short-term request logs (for debugging and rate-limiting): default retention = 7 days, purged unless retention is extended per customer config.
- Debug snapshots & traces (for reproducing incidents): retained up to 90 days by default; snapshot creation is protected and access-controlled.
- Billing & audit metadata (non-content identifiers, usage volumes): retained per billing policy, typically 2 years unless otherwise negotiated.

3) Backups, snapshots & forensic images
- System-level backups and encrypted storage snapshots are created for disaster recovery. Default retention for backups = 180 days.
- Deletion request: we validate regular data stores and live indices within the chosen retention SLA (e.g., 30/90 days), and we schedule deletion in backup windows; forensic backups may remain until their retention expires unless you are on Redwood Private where you control retention and can opt for immediate purge policies.
- For EU residency: backups created in EU regions remain in EU by default when configured; for hosted deployments we offer an EU-only residency option.

4) Deletion SLA options we offer (examples)
- Standard: complete removal from live indices and caches within 30 days; backups purged on normal rotation (up to 180 days).
- Enhanced: live removal within 7 days; coordinated purge from backups within 90 days and additional reporting.
- Private/On-prem: immediate purge possible per your controls; we can provide a customer-managed KMS so we can cryptographically render backups unreadable on request.

5) Edge cases & notes
- Logs used for anomaly detection are aggregated and do not contain raw PII/content by default; we can route logs through a sanitization pipeline on request.
- For legal holds: if GreenPath issues a preservation notice, normal deletion schedules are paused until release.

Attached: deletion-runbook-v1.2.pdf (detailed flow), backup-retention-matrix.xlsx (matrix of default and configurable TTLs), no-train-attestation-signed.pdf

If this fits your needs, Jordan and I can propose specific contract language for the DPA/SOW. Happy to jump on a call with your SOC next week.

Best,
Mina Haddad
Head of Privacy & Compliance | Redwood Inference

Ellen —

Short answers to your SOC follow-ups, plus recommended operational next steps:

1) Proof of deletion for backups
- We provide audit logs for deletion operations (who requested, timestamp, scope). For managed hosted customers, backup purges are driven by retention policies; we can produce retention reports and deletion confirmation when a backup window runs.
- For customers needing cryptographic proof quicker, we offer a "crypto-scrub" option on Private deployments: we revoke or rotate the customer-specific KMS key which renders backups unreadable immediately and we can provide key-rotation evidence.

2) Raw payloads and anomaly detection
- No systems intentionally keep raw full payloads beyond the short-term request logs (default 7 days). If a customer opts into extended debugging traces, those are explicit, access-controlled, and scheduled for deletion within the agreed TTL.
- Aggregated anomaly signals (counts, rate spikes) are stored without payload content and used for platform health only.

3) Enhanced deletion SLA operational cadence
- How it works: customer opens deletion ticket in the Redwood Console or via a signed request to privacy@redwood.com; Redwood Acknowledges within 24 hours; live-index purge completed within the SLA window (7–30 days depending on tier); backup purge aligned to backup rotation, with reporting at completion (we aim for <90 days for Enhanced).

4) Attestation document
- Jordan: I've asked Legal to produce a GreenPath-specific signed attestation (versioned) — we'll attach a signed copy suitable for your audit folder.

Proposal: I'll schedule a 30-minute runbook walkthrough with your SOC and our privacy/ops team early next week. Outline: attestation & wording, deletion workflow, evidence artifacts, and residency configuration.

Thanks,
